text:
Spherical insulating ball and a spherical metallic ball of same size and mass are dropped from the same height. Choose the correct statement out of the following

{Assume negligible air friction}
options: Metal ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the insulating ball
Both will reach the earth's surface simultaneously.
Insulating ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the metal ball
Time taken by them to reach the earth's surface will be independent of the properties of their materials
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The correct answer is option C: the insulating ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the metal ball.

When the two balls are dropped from the same height, they will experience the same gravitational force, which will cause them to accelerate downwards. However, According to Faraday’s law of electromagnetic  induction motion of metal is opposed by earth magnetic  field. Which will slightly reduce its acceleration.

On the other hand, the insulating ball will not experience any electromagnetic  induction. Therefore, it will accelerate downwards at a slightly faster rate than the metal ball. As a result, the insulating ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the metal ball.

So, option C is the correct statement.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: The drift velocity of electrons for a conductor connected in an electrical circuit is $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{d}}$. The conductor is now replaced by another conductor with same material and same length but double the area of cross section. The applied voltage remains same. The new drift velocity of electrons will be
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Same material and length with area $2A$: the new resistance is $R^{'}=\dfrac{ρl}{2A}=\dfrac{R}{2}$, so at the same applied voltage the current doubles, $I^{'}=\dfrac{V}{R^{'}}=2I$.

The free-electron density $n$ is unchanged (same material), so from $I=neAv_{d}$:

$v_{d}^{'}=\dfrac{I^{'}}{ne(2A)}=\dfrac{2I}{2neA}=v_{d}$

The factor $\dfrac{1}{A}$ in $v_{d}=\dfrac{I}{neA}$ is cancelled by the doubled current; the field $E=\dfrac{V}{l}$ that drives the drift is the same in both conductors.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text:
A rod with circular cross-section area $2\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ and length $40\mathrm{cm}$ is wound uniformly with 400 turns of an insulated wire. If a current of $0.4\mathrm{A}$ flows in the wire windings, the total magnetic flux produced inside windings is $4π\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{Wb}$. The relative permeability of the rod is

(Given : Permeability of vacuum $μ_{0}=4π\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{NA}^{-2}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The number of turns per unit length is $n=\dfrac{400}{0.40\text{m}}=1000\text{m}^{-1}$, and $A=2\text{cm}^{2}=2\times 10^{-4}\text{m}^{2}$.

The field inside the rod is $B=μ_{0}μ_{r}nI$, so the flux through the rod is

$\Phi =BA=μ_{0}μ_{r}nIA$

$μ_{r}=\dfrac{\Phi }{μ_{0}nIA}=\dfrac{4π\times 10^{-6}}{4π\times 10^{-7}\times 1000\times 0.4\times 2\times 10^{-4}}$

$μ_{r}=\dfrac{10^{-6}}{8\times 10^{-9}}=125$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: At a certain depth "d " below surface of earth, value of acceleration due to gravity becomes four times that of its value at a height $3\mathrm{R}$ above earth surface. Where $\mathrm{R}$ is Radius of earth (Take $\mathrm{R}=6400\mathrm{km}$ ). The depth $\mathrm{d}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The acceleration due to gravity $g$ at a distance $d$ below the surface of the earth is given by :

$g_{d}=\frac{GM}{R^{3}}(R-d)$

(depth variation)

where $G$ is the gravitational constant and $M$ is the mass of the Earth.

At a height $3R$ above the surface of the Earth, the acceleration due to gravity $g_{h}$ is given by:

$g_{h}=\frac{GM}{(R+3R)^{2}}$

Given, $gd=4gh$ , so we can write :

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{GM}{R^{3}}(R-d)=4\dfrac{GM}{(R+3R)^{2}} \\  \\ \Rightarrow R-d=\dfrac{R}{4} \\  \\ \Rightarrow d=\dfrac{3R}{4} \\  \\ \Rightarrow d=4800\mathrm{km} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: 100 balls each of mass $\mathrm{m}$ moving with speed $v$ simultaneously strike a wall normally and reflected back with same speed, in time $\mathrm{t}\mathrm{s}$. The total force exerted by the balls on the wall is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When the balls strike the wall, the change in momentum of each ball is given by:

$\Delta p=mv-(-mv)=2mv$

 Since there are 100 balls, the total change in momentum of all the balls is $\Delta P=2m(100v)=200mv.$ The time taken for all the balls to strike the wall is $\mathrm{t}$ seconds. Therefore, the average force exerted on the wall is given by:

$F=\frac{\Delta P}{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{2m(100v)}{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{200mv}{\mathrm{t}}$

Therefore, the total force exerted by the balls on the wall is $F=\dfrac{200mv}{\mathrm{t}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text:
A thin rod having a length of $1\mathrm{m}$ and area of cross-section $3\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{m}^{2}$ is suspended vertically from one end. The rod is cooled from $210^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ to $160^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. After cooling, a mass $\mathrm{M}$ is attached at the lower end of the rod such that the length of rod again becomes $1\mathrm{m}$. Young's modulus and coefficient of linear expansion of the rod are $2\times 10^{11}\mathrm{N}\mathrm{m}^{-2}$ and $2\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$, respectively. The value of $\mathrm{M}$ is $__________$ $\mathrm{kg}$.

(Take $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s}^{-2}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When the rod is cooled from 210°C to 160°C, it will contract in length due to thermal contraction. The change in length of the rod is given by:

ΔL = L$α$ΔT

where L is the original length of the rod, α is the coefficient of linear expansion, and ΔT is the change in temperature.

When a mass M is attached to the lower end of the rod, it will stretch due to the weight of the mass. The elongation of the rod is given by:

$\Delta L=\frac{MgL}{AY}$

where M is the mass, g is the acceleration due to gravity, A is the cross-sectional area of the rod, Y is the Young's modulus of the rod, and L is the original length of the rod.

$\therefore$ $Lα\Delta T=\frac{MgL}{AY}$

$\Rightarrow$ $α\Delta T=\frac{Mg}{AY}$

$\Rightarrow$ $Mg=AYα\Delta T$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{M}\times 10=2\times 10^{11}\times 3\times 10^{-6}\times 2\times 10^{-5}\times 50$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{M}=60\mathrm{kg}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

$r_{\text{series}}=r_{1}+r_{2}=2r$

text: An inductor of $0.5\mathrm{mH}$, a capacitor of $20μ\mathrm{F}$ and resistance of $20\Omega$ are connected in series with a $220\mathrm{V}$ ac source. If the current is in phase with the emf, the amplitude of current of the circuit is $\sqrt{x}$ A. The value of $x$ is $___________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$X_{L}=X_{C}$

So, $\mathrm{Z}=\mathrm{R}=20\Omega$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{rms}}=\dfrac{220}{20}=11 \\  \\ \mathrm{i}_{\max }=11\sqrt{2}=\sqrt{242} \end{array}$
